scale.ages: That is {n} times the age of the universe.

scale.trialNote: These rates are generous to the attacker. One real attempt is not one hash: turning a phrase into an address runs PBKDF2 2048 times and then derives keys, which costs thousands of hashes each.

roll.title: Roll your own entropy
roll.lead: Twelve words are a 128-bit number plus a 4-bit checksum. Below you make that number yourself, one throw at a time, and watch it turn into words. Nothing here leaves the page, because there is no network code in this file at all.
roll.leadLink: If the words entropy and checksum are doing no work for you yet, read {link} first.
roll.warn: A phrase generated in a browser is for {em}. For money you intend to keep, generate the phrase on a hardware wallet, or do this on a machine that is offline and stays offline. Never type an existing seed phrase into this or any other page.
roll.disabled: The entropy engine did not load, so this section is disabled.
roll.loadBad: Only 1 to 6 for dice, or 0 and 1 for bits. Letters are not accepted here, and a recovery phrase never should be.
roll.loadLong: That is more than {need} bits. The extra was ignored.
roll.hintDice: Throw a real d6 and press what you see. 1 to 4 carry two bits each. 5 and 6 carry nothing and are thrown again, which is what keeps the sixteen possible pairs equally likely. Backspace undoes the last throw.
roll.hintCoin: Flip a real coin. Heads is 1, tails is 0. Press H or T, or 1 and 0. Backspace undoes the last flip.
roll.wordsLabel: {n} words · each one eleven bits of the {total}-bit total
roll.footnote: These words are exactly as unpredictable as your throws were, and no more. A phrase made in a browser tab is for learning. Put nothing on it that you would mind losing.
pdf.subtitle: The high {c} bits pick a column, the low {r} pick a row, so every word's index is its coordinate on this sheet. The first four letters, set in black, are unique across all 2048; the grey tail is redundant.
ws.noteDice: One die, until {n} boxes are full. Write 1, 2, 3 or 4 in the next box. A 5 or a 6 fills no box, so throw again. Rejecting them is what keeps the four outcomes equally likely.
ws.noteCoin: One coin, {n} times. Heads is 1, tails is 0. Write each result in a box, in order. A flip is already a bit, so there is nothing to convert.
ws.note2: Each throw is two bits: 1 is 00, 2 is 01, 3 is 10, 4 is 11. Fill the cells left to right, top to bottom.
ws.note3: Eleven bits per word. Read the first four bits as a column and the last seven as a row, or the first five and last six on a 32 x 64 sheet. Write the index, then the word.
ws.lastWord: last word carries the checksum, so a machine has to finish this one
ws.foot1: The first {n} words follow from your bits alone, so this sheet and the poster are enough for them.
ws.foot2: The final word mixes the last entropy bits with a SHA-256 checksum. Type your bits into the Roll your own section of this page, with the machine offline, or into a wallet that accepts dice.
ws.foot3: BURN OR SHRED THIS SHEET ONCE THE PHRASE IS RECORDED. IT IS YOUR SEED IN LONGHAND.
